channel.title: Joseph Thomas — Writing
channel.description: Essays on AI agents, swarm intelligence, and systems engineering.

item.title: When AI Becomes Its Own Scientist
item.dc:creator: Joseph Thomas
item.description: Inside the Evolution Arena and the rise of autoresearch. An AI agent that proposes its own experiments, runs them against a live 2D survival simulation, scores the result with a hard mechanical metric, and commits or reverts on its own. A ratchet that only moves forward.

item.title: When Swarms Write Code
item.dc:creator: Joseph Thomas
item.description: How particle swarm optimization escapes the local-minima trap in ARC-AGI. Standard LLM agents get stuck. The fix: a PSO-governed swarm of specialized LLM particles with a continuous fitness function that rewards near-misses. The swarm provides strategy; the LLM provides syntax.

item.title: Stop Wrestling with Boilerplate
item.dc:creator: Joseph Thomas
item.description: Local Tinker — a clean API for local LLM fine-tuning. A Tinker-style API for LoRA fine-tuning of 1B–13B LLMs on your own GPU. Four primitives cover SFT, DPO, PPO, and GRPO without the HuggingFace + PEFT + bitsandbytes boilerplate.

item.title: Building an AI That Masters Snake
item.dc:creator: Joseph Thomas
item.description: A deep reinforcement learning project from scratch. How I built a Snake AI with Deep Q-Learning in PyTorch. A neural network, a shaped reward signal, and a lot of virtual trial and error — no hand-coded strategy, no search algorithms. Averages 44 points over 200 games, peaks at 75.

item.title: Two AIs, One Loop
item.dc:creator: Joseph Thomas
item.description: Building a self-improving code agent. A two-agent architecture — one Claude planning, another implementing, with git diffs and test results flowing between them — captures most of the value of multi-agent coding systems while avoiding their complexity.
